stories.title: Otter.ai raises $320 million from General Catalyst’s growth fund for its meeting tool
stories.simple_summary: Otter.ai, a tool that records and takes notes from meetings, received a large investment of 320 million dollars. The company plans to use this money to expand to more countries and improve its product.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech companies. If you use Otter.ai to record meetings, you might see it improve, but you don't need to do anything about it.

stories.title: Yelp can now call on your behalf to check wait times at a restaurant
stories.simple_summary: Yelp added AI features to its app that can call restaurants for you to check wait times and can remember your favorite types of food. You could potentially have the AI call instead of making the call yourself.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Yelp, this might save you time when deciding where to eat, but it's optional and not something you must use.

stories.title: Mamdani says feds have abdicated on AI, urges New Yorkers to push back
stories.simple_summary: A New York mayor is urging people to demand that the government create rules to control AI. He says people should not accept the idea that AI taking over is unavoidable.
stories.why_it_matters: This is about politics and government, not something that directly affects your daily life right now. Your vote and voice matter if you care about AI regulation.

stories.title: Nscale and Anthropic are reportedly in talks for yet another $45B compute deal
stories.simple_summary: Two companies are discussing a very expensive deal to buy computer power used for building AI systems. This is mostly a business deal between tech companies.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors. There's nothing you need to do.

stories.title: Embedded AI evaluators won’t be an easy solution, Hugging Face’s policy chief says
stories.simple_summary: Experts are discussing whether having outside observers watch AI companies to check for safety problems is actually helpful. The policy chief at a major AI group says it's more complicated than it sounds.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters to people who want AI to be safe, but it's technical and mostly aimed at engineers and government officials.

stories.title: Microsoft says AI agents are like insider threats as ‘frontier models can’t be trusted’
stories.simple_summary: Microsoft is warning business leaders to be careful about AI tools their employees use. Microsoft says these AI tools can pose risks similar to a dishonest employee who might steal information.
stories.why_it_matters: If you run a business and your employees use AI tools, you should think about which tools they use and whether they're secure.

stories.title: The fossil fuel comeback is here
stories.simple_summary: The United States is building more power plants that use coal and natural gas while using more electricity overall. This is happening even though the country is also building more renewable energy like solar and wind.
stories.why_it_matters: This is about energy and climate, not directly about AI. If you care about energy costs or the environment, this affects your future electricity bills and the planet.

stories.title: CoreWeave’s debt is becoming the whole AI industry’s problem
stories.simple_summary: CoreWeave, a company that sells computer power for AI, is having money problems. Its debt became riskier, which makes people worry whether companies building AI systems are spending more money than they can afford.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and large tech companies. If you're not investing in tech stocks, this doesn't directly affect you.

stories.title: Amazon is taking its biggest shot at Nvidia yet with new TorchNeuron dev tool
stories.simple_summary: Amazon created a new tool to help programmers use its own computer chips instead of Nvidia's chips for AI work. Right now Nvidia's chips are the most popular choice.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to engineers and tech companies. It could eventually lead to cheaper AI services, but that impact is far in the future.

stories.title: Hackers hit AI coding tool OpenCode, running up charges on users’ AI accounts
stories.simple_summary: Hackers broke into an AI coding tool called OpenCode and stole passwords that let them use people's AI accounts. This caused charges to run up on users' accounts.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use OpenCode, check your account and change your password immediately. Everyone else should be cautious about which AI tools they trust with their accounts.

stories.title: Tolan snags $30M for its AI companion that helps users navigate life
stories.simple_summary: An AI companion app called Tolan, which helps people with everyday decisions, raised 30 million dollars in new funding. The app already has over 250,000 active users.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors. If you're curious about AI companions that chat with you, Tolan is one option, but you don't need to do anything.

stories.title: Replika’s founder built the AI assistant she pitched at Disrupt 12 years ago
stories.simple_summary: A woman named Eugenia Kuyda started a new AI assistant called Wabi, which is free and available to download. She had the same idea over 12 years ago but is finally launching it now.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're interested in trying a personal AI assistant, Wabi is now available for free. You don't need to do anything unless you want to try it.
